overall_summary: Space-themed cosmic paradoxes and extreme planetary environments (such as burning ice, molten iron, and cosmic oceans) are the clear driving force of the channel's performance. Conversely, repetitive psychological topics and basic animal facts suffer from low engagement and flatline views.

winning_patterns.evidence: The Planet of Burning Ice (vWd0uYcEGh4) achieved 1,053 views, while The Planet Where It Rains Molten Iron (T7iJEp258M8) reached 335 views and 16 likes. The Planet Darker Than Coal (v1rrcZLdp4U) quickly gained 220 views and 15 likes.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme planetary conditions, cosmic anomalies, and space physics paradoxes using highly descriptive, sensory-loaded titles.

winning_patterns.evidence: Why Your Head Is Older Than Your Feet (c_ya3kvpuoI) reached 210 views, and Sharks Are Older Than Trees (bfT7qzZ6aJQ) achieved 302 views.
winning_patterns.action: Produce content that challenges common sense using real physics, biological anomalies, or historical timeline overlaps.

weak_patterns.evidence: Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories (2fqaGqfsR4A) flatlined at 5 views, and The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head (Jc04LVKNd2s) got only 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from generic cognitive psychology facts unless they can be framed as a terrifying mystery or high-stakes survival scenario.
